visual_brief.subject: A four-level model-policy control plane spanning enterprise, team, app, and organization scopes
verified_context: GitHub made GET and PATCH endpoints for Copilot model policies generally available across enterprise, enterprise-team, enterprise-app, and organization scopes.
Policy responses expose configured state, inherited defaults, delegation, and whether lower-level settings are editable or locked.
The policy state at one scope does not by itself determine whether an individual user can access a model.
visual_brief.editorial_idea: One auditable control plane can coordinate model availability across nested scopes without collapsing inherited policy into a single switch.
visual_brief.visual_metaphor: Four nested stone policy plates linked by one adjustable terracotta gate, with locked and delegated layers expressed through physical depth rather than symbols.

candidate_notes.A: Constitution-compliant. The nested rectangular plates make inheritance visible, but the human figure and large rear disc compete with the control mechanism.
candidate_notes.B: Constitution-compliant. The concentric terraces show scope nesting clearly, though the long corridor reads more as access routing than policy editability.
candidate_notes.C: Selected. Four suspended policy plates share one terracotta spindle while physical gaps and blocked arcs express delegated and constrained settings without UI or labels.

crop_review.article_desktop: The four plates, central spindle, and blocked openings remain visible across the wide hero.
crop_review.article_mobile: A centered narrow cover crop retains the terracotta spindle and the three largest policy layers.
crop_review.thumbnail: The stacked silhouette and central terracotta control remain legible at 320px wide.

golden_reference_comparison: The selected image shares the production references' monumental pale geometry, fine linework, restrained terracotta axis, tactile paper field, and confident negative space while remaining specific to layered policy inheritance.
